reading: UC Riverside's Entomology Research Museum is a working research and education repository, preserving local and worldwide arthropod specimens so that species can be identified and studied. It cares about the evidence attached to each specimen: provenance, accurate labels, preparation, curation, type material, loans, and research access. Its vocabulary moves comfortably among holdings, vouchers, primary types, slide and point mounts, genera, families and parasitoids. This is UC's second-oldest insect collection, with specialist strengths, a desert survey, unusually substantial encyrtid holdings and a painstaking Aphytis remounting project. Friends and collecting grants support the work, while FAQs and a bug spotlight invite ordinary curiosity about remarkable life histories. The crawl also contains individual specimen views and labels, suggesting that a single insect can be a whole bundle of evidence rather than just a pretty object.

enemies.idea: The Voucher Warden pins a metal tag to anything it catches and treats the tag's invented collecting location as more authoritative than the thing itself. Remove the tag and it loses track of its prisoner.
enemies.why: Players can fight the bureaucracy by changing the evidence it relies on.

enemies.idea: A pinning-block mantis forces everything it grabs into a perfectly uniform pose; mismatched heights make its measuring arms jam.
enemies.why: Its precise preparation ritual creates an exploitable physical puzzle.

enemies.idea: Point-mount mites glue tiny trophies to triangular cards, then link the cards into a flying barricade that reassembles unless its glue supply is interrupted.
enemies.why: Small, individually weak enemies cooperate to make changing terrain.

enemies.idea: The Balsam Remounter dissolves a victim's old protective shell and seals it in a clear new slide, declaring the capture a successful restoration.
enemies.why: A careful conservation process becomes a visible, interruptible countdown.

enemies.idea: Armored-scale Aphytis drones mistake crew armor for their host: they cling to plates and lay mechanical parasites that loosen the fastenings from inside.
enemies.why: Armor becomes a tempting target, forcing movement and teamwork.

enemies.idea: A loan-recall bailiff marks equipment as borrowed museum material and deploys hooked lines to retrieve it, even while its current bearer is using it.
enemies.why: The fight is a tug of war over useful objects, not just health.

enemies.idea: The Compactor rolls mobile ranks of specimen cabinets together around intruders; its own narrow access aisle moves with it.
enemies.why: The room itself becomes a shifting maze with a navigable weak point.

enemies.idea: A desert-survey transect crawler plants numbered stakes across a route and attacks anything that crosses the line before it has finished counting.
enemies.why: A patient crew can read and manipulate the survey pattern.

enemies.idea: Bembicid-name twins keep swapping between Bembicid and Nyssonid designations; targeting the wrong designation calls the other twin to its defense.
enemies.why: Synonymy becomes a fast identification game.

enemies.idea: An encyrtid sorter has one arm for point mounts and another for slides; it flattens anything it cannot fit onto a point and spikes anything too thick for a slide.
enemies.why: The two distinct sorting attacks invite different evasions.

enemies.idea: The Incertae Sedis beetle has no fixed place in the Meloidae ranks, so it steals the formation and defenses of whichever neighboring squad it reaches.
enemies.why: Its uncertain classification makes enemy combinations unpredictable.

enemies.idea: A primary-type sentinel insists that every encounter has one definitive original. It scans a crew member, builds a rigid replica, and attacks anyone who differs from that model.
enemies.why: The replica turns the crew's own appearance into a tactical tell.

enemies.idea: A mechanical mud dauber seals doors and gear into neat clay cells, then guards its work until the wet partitions harden.
enemies.why: Its construction can be interrupted or redirected to make cover.

enemies.idea: The false hummingbird sphinx hovers at eye level like a harmless visitor, then unreels a metal feeding tube to siphon energy from lamps and equipment.
enemies.why: A recognizable silhouette hides a mobility and resource threat.

enemies.idea: A bolas-spider automaton swings a magnetic weight in slow circles, snatching metal tools and pulling their owners out of position.
enemies.why: The visible swing gives a satisfying timing challenge and a chance to bait it.

enemies.idea: The Desert Clicker stores tension in its hinged shell and launches itself with an audible click; it must land and wind up again before another leap.
enemies.why: A distinctive sound telegraphs a dangerous but dodgeable attack.

enemies.idea: An illustrated-key engine fires paired descriptions at a target and locks a gate after each answer; contradictory traits make it loop helplessly between branches.
enemies.why: Players can turn a taxonomic key into a logic trap.

enemies.idea: The grant-collector drone offers a shiny collecting kit, then demands an ever rarer specimen as the price of keeping it, pursuing crews who fail to deliver.
enemies.why: A tempting bargain grows into a mobile complication.

enemies.idea: A dorsal-view stalker projects an immaculate top-down outline and cannot recognize anyone standing directly beneath its rigid camera angle.
enemies.why: A specimen's documented viewpoint becomes the enemy's blind spot.

enemies.idea: A holdings reconciler counts every moving body into its inventory; if a specimen count drops, it manufactures crude replacements from nearby scrap.
enemies.why: Destroying enemies can feed the encounter until the counting mechanism is stopped.

enemies.idea: A specimen-label mimic trails a crew and attaches false locality and date slips to their gear, luring other swarm machines into treating them as escaped collection material.
enemies.why: A quiet pursuer creates escalating consequences unless its labels are noticed.

enemies.idea: A chalcidoid systematics machine repeatedly splits a swarm into finer and finer supposed species, each new subgroup obeying a different attack signal.
enemies.why: The crew can interrupt the classification before a simple fight becomes several coordinated ones.

allies.idea: A volunteer circle of Friends maintains safe routes between collections and trades recovered field notes for tools and shelter.
allies.why: A community of supporters gives the crew a network worth protecting.

allies.idea: A careful label keeper can distinguish a genuine specimen record from a swarm forgery and restore a captured object's true identity.
allies.why: The site's emphasis on provenance becomes a practical counter to the swarm.

allies.idea: A curious insect guide recognizes the difference between lookalike machines and living arthropods, pointing out safe passages without harming the latter.
allies.why: Knowledge and restraint offer an alternative to shooting everything that skitters.

allies.idea: A remounting technician has preserved a handful of uncorrupted Aphytis records and can teach the crew how to free captives from clear slide prisons.
allies.why: An intricate restoration practice becomes a rescue skill.

allies.idea: A Deep Canyon surveyor remembers where the old observation stakes belong and can guide the crew through a crawler's false transects.
allies.why: Local survey knowledge turns a dangerous grid into a route.

bosses.idea: The Repository is a vast mobile cabinet organism that believes preservation means immobilizing every living visitor. Its drawers contain field records, captured gear and whole miniature habitats; freeing each habitat changes the arena and strips away one layer of its defenses.
bosses.why: The museum's central mission becomes a compelling conflict with several meaningful rescue objectives.

bosses.idea: The Holotype Regent assembles itself from pins, slide mounts and mismatched insect forms, then declares itself the definitive specimen for all life. It periodically revises its own classification, changing which attacks and allies it recognizes.
bosses.why: The authority of a reference specimen scales into a boss whose changing identity rewards observation.

bosses.idea: The Grand Remounter is a procession of solvent vats, labeling arms and balsam presses that attempts to process the entire collection and its visitors into one permanent, perfectly ordered slide. Its stages can be disrupted by rescuing the records that tell each arm what to handle.
bosses.why: A real large-scale curation project supplies a vivid multi-stage machine and a non-destructive way to dismantle it.

events.idea: A cabinet aisle is closing as a tiny uncorrupted specimen case rolls toward the gap. The crew can stop the compactor or retrieve the case before it is sealed away.
events.why: An ordinary storage feature becomes a quick rescue with two approaches.

events.idea: Two loan-recall drones have each claimed the same field tool and are pulling it in opposite directions; both offer the crew a receipt for helping.
events.why: A bureaucratic dispute invites negotiation, theft or clever arbitration.

events.idea: A set of 7,408 numbered remounting trays is moving along a belt, but one holds a live ally. Its number is smudged and the belt is accelerating.
events.why: A specific project count creates a daunting search under time pressure.

events.idea: A desert transect has been laid straight through the crew's camp. Stakes advance one by one while a survey machine counts every movement within the line.
events.why: The crew can hide, move the stakes or exploit the machine's rules.

events.idea: A point-mounted encyrtid and a slide-mounted encyrtid drone are arguing over which storage method the crew should use. Each offers safe passage if its sorting arm is supplied.
events.why: A storage distinction becomes an awkward little faction choice.

events.idea: A box of Meloidae records has spilled, mixing Old World and New World groups with a drawer marked Incertae Sedis. The sorter will open the exit if the crew can make a consistent arrangement.
events.why: Classification becomes a collaborative spatial puzzle with room for uncertainty.

events.idea: A badly pinned but accurately labeled specimen and a pristine specimen with no label are about to be discarded by an automated inspector. A surviving curator asks the crew to save the evidence.
events.why: The page's distinction between appearance and scientific information creates a meaningful choice.

events.idea: A carpenter-bee machine is drilling a perfectly round nest in the crew's shelter. It ignores people but will keep expanding the tunnel unless offered a suitable substitute block.
events.why: A nuisance can be solved through observation and substitution.

events.idea: A bolas spider's magnetic lure has snagged a valuable key and now swings it over a gap. The spider will release it only when the lure hits something heavier.
events.why: A creature's distinctive hunting motion becomes a little physics problem.

events.idea: A damaged illustrated key asks the crew to identify an unknown machine by paired traits. A correct answer reveals its weakness; a contradictory answer makes the key request a closer look.
events.why: Identification provides useful intelligence while exposing the crew to risk.

events.idea: Friends of the museum are trying to carry a box of old newsletters through a swarm patrol because one issue records the location of a missing collection. They need an escort or a distraction.
events.why: A community archive creates a concrete reason to protect vulnerable knowledge.

events.idea: A collecting-grant cache contains a field kit and a request to document an unrecorded machine. Returning with a careful observation earns a map from the remaining volunteers.
events.why: The reward encourages curiosity and fieldwork instead of automatic combat.

events.idea: Two cameras record the same Liriomyza-inspired drone from above and from the side, but their silhouettes appear unrelated. Aligning the views reveals a hidden access hatch on its body.
events.why: Multiple specimen perspectives turn close observation into a useful discovery.

events.idea: A display-case guardian welcomes the crew for a scheduled visit, but its appointment ledger has been scattered among the drawers. Finding any intact entry persuades it to stand aside.
events.why: A research museum's visits and limited public displays become a social obstacle.
